stem.text: Consider the differential equation \( \dfrac{dy}{dx} = x^{2} - y \). Let \( y = f(x) \) be the particular solution with \( f(1) = 3 \). The line tangent to the graph of \( f \) at \( x = 1 \) is \( y = 3 - 2(x - 1) \), and it gives the approximation \( f(1.1) \approx 2.8 \).

parts.prompt: Find the value of \( \dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} \) at the point \( (1, 3) \).

points.criterion: Gives the value 4 for the second derivative at (1, 3).

parts.prompt: Is the approximation \( f(1.1) \approx 2.8 \) an overestimate or an underestimate? Give a reason for your answer.

worked_solution.text: The second derivative is positive at (1, 3), so the graph of f is concave up near x = 1.
A tangent line lies below a concave up graph.

points.criterion: Cites the positive second derivative (concave up near x = 1) and concludes the tangent line lies below the curve, so 2.8 is an underestimate.

parts.prompt: Let \( y = g(x) \) be the particular solution to the same differential equation with \( g(0) = -1 \). Find \( g''(0) \), and determine whether the tangent line approximation \( g(0.3) \approx -0.7 \) is an overestimate or an underestimate. Give a reason for your answer.

worked_solution.text: Negative second derivative means concave down near x = 0, so the tangent line lies above the graph.

points.criterion: Cites g''(0) < 0 (concave down near x = 0) and concludes the tangent line lies above the curve, so -0.7 is an overestimate.
